ospe.Sub_Question_B: Interpret clinical significance when dilation graph crosses Action Line.
ospe.Answer_Key_B: Crossing the Action Line suggests protracted/obstructed labour requiring active management (augmentation, referral, or operative delivery as indicated).
ospe.Sub_Question_C: State four key maternal and fetal parameters recorded on Partograph.

ospe.Title: Station 14
ospe.Scenario_or_Stem: A term newborn is delivered; at 1 minute of life: heart rate >100/min, some flexion of limbs, weak cry, active movements, body pink with blue extremities.
ospe.Sub_Question_A: Calculate the APGAR score at 1 minute based on the five parameters described.
ospe.Answer_Key_A: APGAR components: Appearance (colour), Pulse (heart rate), Grimace (reflex irritability), Activity (muscle tone), Respiration. Based on the description: HR>100=2, some flexion=1, weak cry=1, active movements=2, pink body/blue extremities=1 → total ≈ 7.
ospe.Sub_Question_B: Describe the immediate resuscitation steps you would take based on this score.
ospe.Answer_Key_B: A score of 7 suggests mild depression; provide routine care with close observation, stimulation, and warmth; escalate to bag-mask ventilation only if the score were lower (<7) or condition worsens.
ospe.Sub_Question_C: Discuss the significance of repeating APGAR at 5 minutes and the implications of a persistently low score.

ospe.Title: Station 15
ospe.Scenario_or_Stem: Form 4/4A Medical Certification of Cause of Death: 58-year-old diabetic male who died of Acute Myocardial Infarction following Coronary Artery Thrombosis.
ospe.Sub_Question_A: Fill Part I (a) Immediate Cause, (b) Antecedent Cause, (c) Underlying Cause of Death.
ospe.Answer_Key_A: (a) Immediate cause: Acute Myocardial Infarction; (b) Antecedent cause: Coronary Artery Thrombosis; (c) Underlying cause: the disease/condition that initiated the chain of events leading to death (e.g., coronary artery disease/atherosclerosis).
ospe.Sub_Question_B: Fill Part II (Other significant conditions contributing to death ).
ospe.Answer_Key_B: Diabetes Mellitus is recorded in Part II as a significant condition contributing to death but not part of the direct causal sequence.
ospe.Sub_Question_C: State importance of underlying cause of death in mortality coding (ICD-11).

ospe.Title: Station 16
ospe.Scenario_or_Stem: Assessment of nutritional status in 2-year-old child using Shakir MUAC tape .
ospe.Sub_Question_A: Demonstrate anatomical landmark and placement technique for MUAC measurement.
ospe.Answer_Key_A: Landmark: midpoint between the tip of the shoulder (acromion) and tip of the elbow (olecranon) on the left arm, with the arm relaxed at the side.
ospe.Sub_Question_B: State the colour-zone cut-off values used to classify a child's nutritional status by MUAC (SAM/MAM/Normal), and interpret their significance.
ospe.Answer_Key_B: Red (<11.5cm) = Severe Acute Malnutrition; Yellow (11.5–12.5cm) = Moderate Acute Malnutrition; Green (>12.5cm) = Normal nutritional status.
ospe.Sub_Question_C: State advantages of MUAC as a quick community screening tool.

ospe.Title: Station 17
ospe.Scenario_or_Stem: Counselling a postpartum mother choosing Injectable Medroxyprogesterone Acetate (DMPA 150 mg).
ospe.Sub_Question_A: State the recommended dose, route, and frequency of administration of DMPA.
ospe.Answer_Key_A: 150mg, Intramuscular (deep), every 3 months (12 weeks).
ospe.Sub_Question_B: Describe the mechanism of action of DMPA.
ospe.Answer_Key_B: Mechanism: suppresses ovulation (anovulation), thickens cervical mucus to block sperm entry, and causes endometrial atrophy unfavourable to implantation.
ospe.Sub_Question_C: Address the common side-effect counselling points you would discuss with this mother.

ospe.Title: Station 18
ospe.Scenario_or_Stem: Identification of Comprehensive Primary Health Care (CPHC) service package at Ayushman Arogya Mandir (Health and Wellness Centre).
ospe.Sub_Question_A: List 12 packages of CPHC services delivered at Ayushman Arogya Mandir.
ospe.Answer_Key_A: 12 CPHC packages include: care in pregnancy & childbirth; neonatal & infant health; childhood & adolescent health; family planning & contraceptive services; management of communicable diseases (NPs); management of NCDs; screening & management of common cancers; care for common ophthalmic/ENT conditions; basic oral health care; care for elderly/palliative care; mental health; emergency medical services.
ospe.Sub_Question_B: Role of Community Health Officer (CHO) and ASHA in NCD screening (CBAC form).
ospe.Answer_Key_B: CHO leads NCD screening at the AAM using the CBAC (Community-Based Assessment Checklist) form; ASHA supports community mobilization, follow-up, and referral linkage.
ospe.Sub_Question_C: Explain e-Sanjeevani tele-consultation platform workflow.

ospe.Title: Station 19
ospe.Scenario_or_Stem: During a school health screening camp, a 10-year-old child is noted to squint frequently, sits at the front of the classroom by choice, and complains of headache while trying to read the blackboard from a distance.
ospe.Sub_Question_A: 1) Demonstrate correct technique and distance for Snellen's chart testing. 2) Perform and record this child's visual acuity. 3) List common causes of refractive error in school children. 4) State criteria for referral. 5) Mention components of eye screening under the school health programme.
ospe.Answer_Key_A: Snellen's chart placed at 6 metres, one eye tested at a time with the other covered; visual acuity recorded as a fraction (distance tested/distance at which a normal eye reads that line).
ospe.Sub_Question_B: escribe how you would counsel the parents and refer this child for further ophthalmic evaluation.
ospe.Answer_Key_B: Confirm with repeated readings on separate occasions and/or out-of-office measurement (home BP monitoring or ambulatory BP monitoring) before diagnosing hypertension, per standard guidelines.
ospe.Sub_Question_C: Discuss the National Programme for Control of Blindness and Visual Impairment (NPCBVI) and its role in school eye screening.

ospe.Title: Station 20
ospe.Scenario_or_Stem: A 45-year-old man presents to PHC for a routine health check. On examination using a mercury sphygmomanometer, BP is recorded as 148/94 mmHg on the right arm in sitting position.
ospe.Sub_Question_A:
1) Demonstrate the correct technique and precautions for BP measurement using a sphygmomanometer. 
2) Classify this reading according to current hypertension guidelines. 
3) State the cuff size selection criteria. 
4) List common errors in BP measurement.
5) State the recommended repeat measurement protocol.
ospe.Answer_Key_A: Correct technique: seated position, arm at heart level, appropriate cuff size, rest 5 minutes before measurement, avoid caffeine/smoking before reading. Classification: Stage 2 hypertension (≥160/100 mmHg... here 148/94 falls in Stage 1/Grade 1, ≥130/80 and <140/90 per some guidelines — apply the specific national/JNC classification in use). Cuff size: bladder should cover 80% of arm circumference. Common errors: wrong cuff size, unsupported arm, talking during measurement. Repeat protocol: average of 2 readings, 1-2 minutes apart.
ospe.Sub_Question_B: Describe how you would confirm the diagnosis of hypertension in this patient  before labelling him hypertensive.
ospe.Sub_Question_C: Discuss population-based and opportunistic screening for hypertension under NP-NCD at the primary care level.

spotter.Title: Spotter 1
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the specimen  and mention its identifying features.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: boat-shaped eggs laid singly on the water surface, each with lateral floats
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State its breeding habitat/site.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: clean, stagnant water collections
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss the public health importance of this pre-larval stage and its relevance to the vector control programme.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Control measure: indoor residual spraying and insecticide-treated nets; relevant programme: NVBDCP.

spotter.Title: Spotter 2
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the specimen and mention two features that help identify it.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: a hard dorsal scutum covering the body
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State the disease(s) associated with this specimen.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Kyasanur Forest Disease and spotted fever
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss the control measures applicable to this specimen, including the relevant programme.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: acaricide use and protective clothing; relevant programme: forest-area vector surveillance.

spotter.Title: Spotter 3
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the food item and state its predominant nutrient class.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Rice, Cereal
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State its nutritive value per 100g( cooked )and deficient amino acids
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Per 100g of white rice (long‑grain, cooked), the nutritive value is about 130kcal energy, 28g carbohydrates, and 2.7–3g protein; low in protein quality (lysine)
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss its role in a public health nutrition programme or in preventing a specific nutritional deficiency disorder.

spotter.Title: Spotter 4
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the food item and Name the microorganism responsible for curd formation.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Curd
spotter.Sub_Question_B: What is the biochemical process involved in curd formation? And Mention one public health relevance of curd consumption.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: fermented milk product; source of probiotics
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Explain how curd consumption can influence the gut microbiome and its role in preventing antibiotic‑associated diarrhea and micronutrient deficiency.

spotter.Title: Spotter 5
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the vaccine and state the UIP schedule/programme it belongs to.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State its dose, route, and schedule as applicable.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: given intradermal at birth (0.05) LUA over deltoid insertion, protects against severe forms of childhood TB
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss a relevant programmatic aspect associated with it (cold chain, AEFI, wastage, or VVM interpretation).

spotter.Title: Spotter 6
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the item shown and What is the main purpose of an AD syringe?
spotter.Answer_Key_A: AD syringe, It prevents reuse by automatically locking or disabling after a single use, ensuring injection safety.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: Explain how AD syringes help in both infection control and public health programs.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: By preventing reuse, AD syringes reduce transmission of blood‑borne infections (HIV, hepatitis B/C). Their use in immunization programs ensures safe injections, builds public trust, and supports WHO’s safe injection policy.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Why are AD syringes considered essential in mass immunization campaigns compared to conventional disposable syringes?

spotter.Title: Spotter 7
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the contraceptive shown and state its category.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: intrauterine device
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State its mechanism of action, schedule,and absolute contraindications.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: 10-year effective lifespan
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss its advantages, disadvantages, or contraindications (WHO MEC category) relevant to client counselling.

spotter.Title: Spotter 8
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the tool shown and the method it is used with.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Cervical Mucus Chart. It is used with the Billings Ovulation Method
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State its use and the information it helps track or communicate.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: The chart records changes in cervical mucus consistency (dry, sticky, creamy, watery, stretchy/“egg‑white”), which helps track fertile and infertile phases of the menstrual cycle. It communicates ovulation timing for fertility awareness, either to achieve or avoid pregnancy.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss counselling points relevant to correct use of the cervical mucus chart.

spotter.Title: Spotter 9
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the specimen (with chemical formula) shown. State one common use of bleaching powder in public health.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Bleaching Powder (Calcium Oxychloride, CaOCl₂). It is used for disinfection of drinking water.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: Explain how bleaching powder acts as a disinfectant and mention one limitation.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Bleaching powder releases chlorine when mixed with water, which kills pathogenic microorganisms. However, excess chlorine can cause taste and odor problems and may form harmful by‑products.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Why is bleaching powder preferred in rural water supply schemes compared to liquid chlorine?

spotter.Title: Spotter 10
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the organization represented by the emblem shown. State the year in which WHO was established.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: World Health Organization (WHO). 1948
spotter.Sub_Question_B: Mention two major functions of WHO in global health.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Sets international health standards and guidelines. Provides technical support and coordinates responses to health emergencies.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Why is WHO’s International Health Regulations (IHR) critical for global disease control?
spotter.Answer_Key_C: These legally binding rules require countries to report public health emergencies of international concern (like pandemics), enabling rapid global response and reducing cross‑border spread of diseases.

spotter.Title: Spotter 11
spotter.Sub_Question_A: For the scenario 'Road traffic accident involving a helmetless two-wheeler rider', identify the three phases of the Haddon Matrix.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Pre-event, event, and post-event phases.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: List one host factor, one agent/vehicle factor, and one environmental factor relevant to this scenario.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Propose one preventive intervention applicable to each phase of the Haddon Matrix for this scenario.
spotter.Remarks: Set 1 Spotter 11 – Haddon Matrix: Road traffic accident involving a helmetless two-wheeler rider

spotter.Title: Spotter 1
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the specimen and describe one visible feature
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Anopheles larva — lies parallel to water surface, lacks siphon tube.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: 1. Compare its resting position in water with another mosquito larva. 2. Explain why this stage is important in disease transmission.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Culex hangs at angle; Anopheles lies flat. Larval stage is critical in malaria transmission.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Suggest combined strategy to control this larval stage.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Environmental management + biological control + NVBDCP measures.

spotter.Title: Spotter 2
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the specimen and mention one structural trait
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Soft tick (Argasid) — wrinkled body, no dorsal scutum.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: 1. Name a disease linked to this vector. 2. Explain how its feeding habits affect detection.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Tick‑borne relapsing fever. Nocturnal burrow feeding complicates surveillance.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Propose ecological measure to reduce infestations.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Rodent population reduction and burrow treatment.

spotter.Title: Spotter 3
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the food item and its nutrient group
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Wheat — cereal, carbohydrate source.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: 1. Name the protein complex responsible for dough elasticity. 2. State one limitation of its protein quality.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Gluten (gliadin + glutenin). Deficient in lysine.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Explain how fortification addresses a major deficiency.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Fortification with iron, folic acid, B12 combats anemia.

spotter.Title: Spotter 4
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the food item and its nutrient group
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Ghee — fat.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: 1. List the fat‑soluble vitamins carried by this food. 2. State one benefit and one risk of consumption.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Vitamins A, D, E, K. Benefit: vitamin absorption; Risk: obesity/CVD.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss its role in traditional diets compared to modern health concerns.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Traditionally valued for energy; modern caution due to saturated fat.

spotter.Title: Spotter 5
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the vaccine and its dose and route of administration
spotter.Answer_Key_A: MR vaccine — protects against measles & rubella.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: 1. State the ages at which it is given under UIP. 2. Mention one storage requirement.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: 9–12 months & 16–24 months. Stored at +2 °C to +8 °C, protected from light.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Explain why this vaccine was introduced in India.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Eliminates measles, controls congenital rubella syndrome.

spotter.Title: Spotter 6
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the equipment
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Ice pack — used in vaccine carriers.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: 1. Describe how it is prepared before use. 2. Explain its role in vaccine safety.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Frozen then conditioned until droplets appear. Maintains cold chain temperature.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: State one error that can occur if preparation is incorrect.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Freezing vaccines like DPT/TT reduces potency.

spotter.Title: Spotter 7
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the contraceptive device and its category
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Cu‑T 375 — intrauterine device.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: 1. State its effective lifespan. 2. Mention one advantage and one disadvantage.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Lifespan 5 years. Advantage: long‑term, reversible; Disadvantage: heavier periods.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Outline counselling points for insertion and removal.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Counselling: insertion during menses, check strings monthly, removal by trained provider.

spotter.Title: Spotter 8
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the counselling aid and the method it supports
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Withdrawal counselling card — coitus interruptus method.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: 1. Explain why this method is unreliable. 2. Mention one precaution for couples using it.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Pre‑ejaculatory sperm risk. Requires strong partner cooperation.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Compare its failure rate with barrier methods.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Failure ~20%; higher than condoms (~2–12%).

spotter.Title: Spotter 9
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the item and describe its general purpose
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Chlorine tablets — used for water disinfection.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: Explain how this item is typically used at the household level. Mention one advantage and one limitation of its use.
spotter.Answer_Key_B:
Added to water in recommended doses (e.g., per bucket or container).
Advantage: simple and portable; Limitation: taste/odor issues.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Explain its importance in disaster situations.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Critical in disaster relief camps to prevent cholera/diarrhea.

spotter.Title: Spotter 10
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the organization and year of establishment
spotter.Answer_Key_A: UNICEF — established 1946.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: 1. State its primary focus. 2. Mention one programme it supports in India.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Focus: child health, nutrition, welfare. Programme: immunization, maternal‑child health.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Explain its role in global child survival strategies.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Global strategies: immunization, nutrition, safe water.

spotter.Title: Spotter 11
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify two host factors
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Web of Causation – Type 2 Diabetes — host factors: obesity, sedentary lifestyle.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: 1. Mention one environmental factor. 2. Explain how multiple causes interact.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Environment: urbanization, high‑calorie diet. Causes interact → insulin resistance.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Outline prevention strategies at primary, secondary, and tertiary levels.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Primary: lifestyle modification. Secondary: screening. Tertiary: complication management.
spotter.Remarks: Set 2 Spotter 11 – Web of Causation: Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus

spotter.Title: Spotter 1
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the specimen and describe one visible feature
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Anopheles adult — spotted wings, rests at 45° angle.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State one disease linked to this vector. Explain how its resting posture helps recognition.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Disease: malaria. Resting posture at angle is diagnostic.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss one national programme strategy targeting this vector.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Indoor residual spraying and insecticide‑treated nets under NVBDCP.

spotter.Title: Spotter 2
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the specimen and describe one visible feature
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Bed bug — flat, reddish‑brown, nocturnal insect.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State one health effect associated with this insect. Explain why it is considered a nuisance pest.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Causes skin irritation, sleeplessness. Nuisance due to nocturnal biting.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Suggest one control measure relevant to household infestation.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Mattress treatment, heat treatment; part of general pest control.

spotter.Title: Spotter 3
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the food item and its nutrient group
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Ragi — cereal/millet.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State one nutrient for which this cereal is notable. Explain its relevance in diets.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Rich source of calcium. Important in staple diets.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss its role in preventing a specific deficiency disorder.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Helps prevent calcium deficiency and rickets.

spotter.Title: Spotter 4
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the food item and its nutrient group
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Jaggery — sweetener.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State one micronutrient present in this sweetener. Explain how it differs from refined sugar.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Contains trace iron.refined sugar is highly processed, purified sucrose stripped of everything but sweetness.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss its role in addressing nutritional deficiencies.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Helps prevent iron deficiency anemia in populations relying on sugar.

spotter.Title: Spotter 5
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the vaccine and strains of the agent used
spotter.Answer_Key_A: OPV — oral polio vaccine.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State the route of administration. Mention the ages when it is given under UIP.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Oral route. Given at birth and with each DPT dose.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Explain one programmatic aspect critical for its use.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Cold chain maintenance and VVM interpretation are essential.

spotter.Title: Spotter 6
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the equipment
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Day carrier — used for short‑duration vaccine transport.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State its primary use. Explain how long it can maintain vaccine temperature.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Maintains temperature for a few hours. Ensures potency during sessions.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss its role in outreach immunization sessions.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Enables safe vaccine delivery in field immunization.

spotter.Title: Spotter 7
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the contraceptive device and its category
spotter.Answer_Key_A: LNG‑IUS — intrauterine system, hormone‑releasing.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State its mechanism of action. Mention one therapeutic use.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Releases levonorgestrel, inhibits endometrium. Used for menorrhagia.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss counselling points for clients considering this device.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Counselling: effective for 5 years, may cause irregular bleeding, contraindicated in pelvic infection.

spotter.Title: Spotter 8
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the tool and the method it supports
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Rhythm chart — tracks menstrual cycle.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State what information it helps track. Explain how it is used in fertility awareness.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Tracks fertile and infertile days. Used for fertility awareness.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss counselling points for correct use.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Requires regular cycles, partner cooperation, abstinence during fertile days.

spotter.Title: Spotter 9
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the equipment
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Horrocks apparatus — estimates chlorine demand of water.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State its purpose. Explain how it is used in water testing.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Used to determine chlorine requirement. Ensures correct dosage.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss its public health significance.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Prevents under‑ or over‑chlorination; ensures safe drinking water.

spotter.Title: Spotter 10
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the organization
spotter.Answer_Key_A: UNFPA — established 1969.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State year of establishment. Mention its primary focus.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Focus: reproductive health and population programmes.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Explain its role in India’s reproductive health programmes.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Supports family planning and reproductive health initiatives in India.

spotter.Title: Spotter 11
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the scenario phases
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Haddon Matrix – Drowning in unfenced pond — phases: pre‑event, event, post‑event.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State one host, one agent and one environmental factor.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Host: child unsupervised. Environment: unfenced pond.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Propose preventive interventions for each phase.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Pre‑event: fencing ponds. Event: supervision. Post‑event: resuscitation and emergency care.
spotter.Remarks: Set 3 Spotter 11 – Haddon Matrix: Drowning of a child in an unfenced pond

spotter.Title: Spotter 1
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the specimen and describe one visible feature
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Culex egg — raft‑like clusters floating on water.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State one typical breeding site. Explain why this stage is important in disease transmission.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Breeds in polluted or stagnant water and drains. Eggs mark the start of mosquito life cycle linked to filariasis/encephalitis.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Suggest one control measure relevant to this stage.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Source reduction of polluted water bodies; NVBDCP strategy.

spotter.Title: Spotter 2
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the specimen and describe one visible feature
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Cockroach — flattened body, nocturnal habits.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State one health risk associated with this insect. Explain why it is considered a household pest.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Mechanical transmission of enteric pathogens. Household nuisance due to contamination.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Suggest one sanitation‑based control measure.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Sanitation and insecticidal gel baiting; general sanitation programme.

spotter.Title: Spotter 3
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the food item and its nutrient group
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Maize — cereal.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State one amino acid deficiency. Explain why it is energy‑dense.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Deficient in lysine and tryptophan. High carbohydrate content.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss its role in preventing a nutritional deficiency disorder.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Linked to pellagra prevention when combined with pulses.

spotter.Title: Spotter 4
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the food item and its nutrient group
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Groundnut — nut/oilseed.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State one nutrient it provides. Explain why it is considered a good protein source; (calorie and protein in 100gm)
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Provides vegetable protein and fat. Rich in calories. 567 kcal and 25–26 g protein per 100 g.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss its role in preventing malnutrition.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Helps prevent protein‑energy malnutrition.

spotter.Title: Spotter 5
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the vaccine, strain, dose and schedule
spotter.Answer_Key_A: IPV — inactivated polio vaccine.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State the route of administration. Mention its role in eradication strategy.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Intramuscular route. Used in polio eradication.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Explain one programmatic aspect critical for its use.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Cold chain maintenance and monitoring of wastage.

spotter.Title: Spotter 6
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the equipment and its mechanism
spotter.Answer_Key_A: A cold box is an insulated, non-electric container used to store or transport vaccines short-term at 4–8°C using ice packs.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State its primary use. Explain where it is placed in the cold chain.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: It sits at the peripheral cold chain level, used between PHC/Sub-Centre for short transport, outreach sessions, or as backup storage during power failures.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss its role in immunization programme.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Ensures safe vaccine storage during transport.

spotter.Title: Spotter 7
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the contraceptive method
spotter.Answer_Key_A: DMPA (Antara) injectable contraceptive.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State its schedule. Mention one advantage and one disadvantage.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Administered every 3 months. Advantage: long‑term, reversible; Disadvantage: menstrual irregularities.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Outline counselling points for correct use.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Counselling: adherence to schedule, possible side effects, contraindications.

spotter.Title: Spotter 8
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the tool and the method it supports
spotter.Answer_Key_A: NSV counselling model — used for No‑Scalpel Vasectomy.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State its purpose. Explain how it is used in counselling.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Demonstrates procedure to clients. Helps in informed choice.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss one precaution for correct use.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Counselling: permanent method, requires consent, post‑procedure care.

spotter.Title: Spotter 9
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the equipment
spotter.Answer_Key_A: H₂S water test kit — field‑level bacteriological test.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State its purpose. Explain how it is used in water testing.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Detects contamination in drinking water. Simple household‑level test.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss its public health significance.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Ensures safe water supply; supports surveillance guidelines.
spotter.Remarks: Set 4 Spotter 9 – H2S water test kit

spotter.Title: Spotter 10
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the organization
spotter.Answer_Key_A: NTEP — National TB Elimination Programme.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State its primary objective. Mention its role in India.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Objective: TB elimination. Role: nationwide TB control.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Explain its contribution to TB elimination.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Provides diagnosis, treatment, and monitoring under India’s TB strategy.

spotter.Title: Spotter 11
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the scenario phases
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Web of causation – Coronary Heart Disease
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State one host factor. Mention one environmental factor.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Host: smoking, obesity. Environment: sedentary lifestyle, stress.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Propose preventive interventions for each phase.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Pre‑event: lifestyle modification. Event: emergency response. Post‑event: rehabilitation and secondary prevention.
spotter.Remarks: Set 4 Spotter 11 – Web of Causation: Coronary Heart Disease

spotter.Title: Spotter 1
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the specimen and describe one visible feature
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Culex larva — long siphon tube.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State one typical breeding site. Explain why this stage is important in disease transmission.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Breeds in polluted or stagnant water and drains. Larval stage linked to filariasis and encephalitis transmission.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Suggest one control measure relevant to this stage.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Source reduction of polluted water bodies; NVBDCP strategy.

spotter.Title: Spotter 2
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the specimen and describe one visible feature
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Body/head louse — dorsoventrally flattened, wingless insect.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: Name one disease associated with this insect. Explain why it is epidemiologically important.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Epidemic typhus, relapsing fever, trench fever. Important in outbreaks due to close contact transmission.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Suggest one control measure relevant to epidemic situations.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Personal hygiene and delousing measures; outbreak control programmes.

spotter.Title: Spotter 3
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the food item and its nutrient group
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Bengal gram (chana dal) — pulse.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State one limiting amino acid. Explain why it is considered a good protein source(protein and calorie content (raw)) .
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Limiting amino acid: methionine. Provides good protein(364 kcal and 17–20 g protein per 100 g (raw)).
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss its role in preventing malnutrition.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Helps prevent protein‑energy malnutrition when combined with cereals.

spotter.Title: Spotter 4
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the food item and its nutrient group
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Sesame seeds — oilseed.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State one nutrient it provides. Explain why it is considered energy‑dense. (calorie and fat per 100gm)
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Rich in calcium and fat. High energy content. 570–575 kcal and 50g fat per 100 g.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss its role in preventing a nutritional deficiency disorder.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Helps prevent calcium deficiency and supports bone health.

spotter.Title: Spotter 5
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the vaccine, dose and schedule
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Pentavalent vaccine — protects against diphtheria, pertussis, tetanus, Hepatitis B, Hib.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State the diseases it protects against. Mention the route of administration. Which component causes fever.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Intramuscular route. Combines multiple antigens.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Explain one programmatic aspect critical for its use.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Cold chain maintenance and monitoring of wastage.

spotter.Title: Spotter 6
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the equipment
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Twin bag system — separates vaccines needing freezing from those that must not freeze.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State its primary use. Explain why it is important in vaccine storage.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Prevents accidental freezing of sensitive vaccines. Ensures correct storage.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss its role in immunization programme.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Maintains vaccine potency and safety during cold chain management.

spotter.Title: Spotter 7
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the contraceptive method and route
spotter.Answer_Key_A: sayana press — injectable contraceptive.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State its schedule. Mention one advantage and one disadvantage.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Sayana Press is administered once every 12 to 13 weeks (approximately three months) to provide effective contraception, with the main advantage being convenient long-term pregnancy prevention and one key disadvantage being possible irregular menstrual changes or delay in return to fertility.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Outline counselling points for correct use.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Counselling: adherence to schedule, possible side effects, contraindications.

spotter.Title: Spotter 8
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the tool and the method it supports
spotter.Answer_Key_A: LAM counselling card — supports Lactational Amenorrhea Method.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State its purpose. Explain how it is used in counselling.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Explains criteria for postpartum contraception. Used for first 6 months postpartum.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss one precaution for correct use.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Counselling: exclusive breastfeeding, amenorrhea, infant <6 months.

spotter.Title: Spotter 9
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the equipment
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Portable chlorinator — continuous chlorination of small water supplies.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State its purpose. Explain how it is used in water treatment.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Provides safe drinking water. Used in small community supplies.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss its public health significance.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Prevents waterborne diseases; supports safe water guidelines.

spotter.Title: Spotter 10
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the organization
spotter.Answer_Key_A: NLEP — National Leprosy Eradication Programme, launched 1983.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State its primary objective. Mention its role in India.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Objective: leprosy elimination. Role: nationwide control.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Explain its contribution to disease elimination.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Provides diagnosis, MDT treatment, and monitoring under India’s leprosy strategy.

spotter.Title: Spotter 11
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the scenario (Domestic burn injury from an open cooking stove) phases of haddon matrix
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Haddon Matrix – Domestic burn injury from open stove — phases: pre‑event, event, post‑event.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: List one host factor, one agent/vehicle factor, and one environmental factor relevant to this scenario.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Host: child near stove. Environment: unsafe cooking practices.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Propose preventive interventions for each phase.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Pre‑event: safer stove design. Event: fire safety response. Post‑event: burn care and rehabilitation.
spotter.Remarks: Set 5 Spotter 11 – Haddon Matrix: Domestic burn injury from an open cooking stove

spotter.Title: Spotter 1
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the specimen and describe one visible feature
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Culex adult — unspotted wings, rests parallel to surface.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State one disease linked to this vector. Explain how its resting posture helps recognition.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Diseases: lymphatic filariasis, Japanese encephalitis. Resting parallel helps distinguish from Anopheles.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss one national programme strategy targeting this vector.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Source reduction of polluted water bodies; targeted under NVBDCP.

spotter.Title: Spotter 2
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the specimen and describe one visible feature
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Rat flea (Xenopsylla cheopis) — laterally flattened, jumping insect.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State one disease associated with this vector. Explain why its ecology makes control difficult.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Disease: plague. Ecology: thrives in rodent burrows.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Suggest one control measure relevant to endemic areas.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Rodent control and insecticidal dusting of burrows; plague surveillance programme.

spotter.Title: Spotter 3
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the food item and its nutrient group
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Green gram (moong dal) — pulse.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State one reason it is considered efor early weaning or during illness. Mention one limiting amino acid.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: low content of complex oligosaccharides and antinutritional factors (like trypsin inhibitors) compared to other legumes, and its outer coat/husk is thin, making it easier to break down and digest. Limiting amino acid: methionine.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss its role in preventing malnutrition.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Helps prevent protein‑energy malnutrition when combined with cereals.

spotter.Title: Spotter 4
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the food item and its nutrient group
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Iodized salt — fortified food.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State its fortification purpose. Maximum amount taken per day to prevent hypentension
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Vehicle for iodine fortification. < 5gm/day
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss its role in national nutrition programmes.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Used in IDD control programmes to prevent goitre and cretinism.

spotter.Title: Spotter 5
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the vaccine, dose and schedule
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Rotavirus vaccine — oral vaccine.
spotter.Sub_Question_B:
State the route of administration.
Describe the type of illness it protects against.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Prevents severe rotavirus diarrhoea. Oral route.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Explain one programmatic aspect critical for its use.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Cold chain maintenance and monitoring of AEFI.

spotter.Title: Spotter 6
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the equipment
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Tally sheet — used to record doses.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State its primary use. Explain how it is filled during sessions.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Records daily doses administered. Filled during immunization sessions.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss its role in immunization programme.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Ensures accountability and monitoring of vaccine coverage.

spotter.Title: Spotter 7
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the contraceptive method
spotter.Answer_Key_A: ECP — emergency contraceptive pill, hormonal method.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State its timing of use. Mention one advantage and one disadvantage.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Used within 72 hours of unprotected intercourse. Advantage: prevents pregnancy; Disadvantage: irregular bleeding.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Outline counselling points for correct use.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Counselling: not for regular use, contraindications, must be taken promptly.

spotter.Title: Spotter 8
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the tool and the method it supports
spotter.Answer_Key_A: NSV kit — instrument set for No‑Scalpel Vasectomy.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State its purpose. Explain how it is used in counselling.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Used for minimally invasive male sterilization. Demonstrates procedure.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss one precaution for correct use.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Counselling: permanent method, requires consent, post‑procedure care.

spotter.Title: Spotter 9
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the equipment
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Alum sedimentation jar — used to demonstrate coagulation‑sedimentation. Rapid
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State its purpose. Explain how it is used in water treatment. Which type of sand filter it is used?
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Shows removal of turbidity in water. Demonstrates treatment process.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss its public health significance.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Ensures safe drinking water; supports water safety guidelines.

spotter.Title: Spotter 10
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the organization
spotter.Answer_Key_A: NVBDCP — National Vector Borne Disease Control Programme.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State its primary objective. Mention its role in India.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Objective: control malaria, dengue, filariasis, etc. Role: umbrella programme for vector diseases.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Explain its contribution to vector‑borne disease control.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Provides integrated surveillance, prevention, and treatment nationwide.

spotter.Title: Spotter 11
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the scenario phases
spotter.Answer_Key_A: web of causation – Childhood obesity — phases: pre‑event, event, post‑event.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State one host factor. Mention one environmental factor.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Host: sedentary lifestyle. Environment: unhealthy diet, urbanization.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss primary, secondary, and tertiary prevention strategies based on this web of causation for Childhood Obesity.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Pre‑event: promote healthy diet/exercise. Event: early detection and counselling. Post‑event: management of complications.
spotter.Remarks: Set 6 Spotter 11 – Web of Causation: Childhood Obesity

spotter.Title: Spotter 1
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the specimen and describe one visible feature
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Aedes larva — short siphon with single row of comb scales.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State one typical breeding site. Explain why this stage is important in disease transmission.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Breeds in clean water containers, tyres, coolers. Larval stage linked to dengue, chikungunya transmission.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Suggest control measure relevant to this stage.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Source reduction of container breeding sites; weekly dry day under NVBDCP.

spotter.Title: Spotter 2
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the specimen and describe one visible feature
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Trombiculid mite (chigger) — six‑legged parasitic larval stage.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: Name one disease associated with this vector. Explain why its habitat makes control challenging.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Disease: scrub typhus. Habitat: scrub vegetation.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Suggest one preventive measure relevant to endemic areas.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: DEET‑based repellents and clearance of scrub vegetation; NVBDCP surveillance.

spotter.Title: Spotter 3
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the food item and its nutrient group
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Red gram (arhar/tur dal) — pulse.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State one limiting amino acid. Explain why it is considered a good protein source (calorie and protein in 100gm (raw)).
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Limiting amino acid: methionine. Provides good protein. 335–343 kcal and 20–22 g protein per 100 g (raw)
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss its role in preventing malnutrition.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Helps prevent protein‑energy malnutrition when combined with cereals.

spotter.Title: Spotter 4
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the food item and its nutrient group
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Amla — fruit.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State one vitamin it is rich in. Explain its relevance in diets.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Exceptionally rich in vitamin C. Improves immunity.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss its role in preventing a nutritional deficiency disorder.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Prevents scurvy and supports micronutrient sufficiency.

spotter.Title: Spotter 5
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the vaccine, dose and schedule
spotter.Answer_Key_A: PCV — pneumococcal conjugate vaccine.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State the route of administration. Mention the type of illness it protects against.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Intramuscular route. Protects against pneumonia and meningitis.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Explain  programmatic aspect critical for its use.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Cold chain maintenance and monitoring of AEFI.

spotter.Title: Spotter 6
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the equipment
spotter.Answer_Key_A: MCP card — Mother and Child Protection card.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State its primary use. Explain what information it records.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Records immunization and maternal health status. Used for tracking services.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss its role in maternal and child health programmes.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Ensures continuity of care and monitoring in public health programmes.

spotter.Title: Spotter 7
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the contraceptive method
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Male condom — barrier method.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State its category. Mention one advantage and one disadvantage.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Dual protection against pregnancy and STI/HIV. Advantage: accessible; Disadvantage: may reduce sensation.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Outline counselling points for correct use.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Counselling: consistent use, disposal, STI protection emphasized.

spotter.Title: Spotter 8
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the tool and the method it supports
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Falope ring — used in laparoscopic tubal occlusion.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State its purpose. Explain explain cafeteria approach
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Demonstrates permanent female sterilization method. All choices with pro and cons.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss one precaution for correct use.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Counselling: permanent method, requires consent, surgical risks explained.

spotter.Title: Spotter 9
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the equipment
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Slow sand filter model — community‑level water filtration.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: Name and role of bacterial layer. Explain how it is used in water treatment.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Removes suspended matter and pathogens. Demonstrates safe water supply.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss its public health significance.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Ensures potable water; supports rural water safety programmes.
spotter.Remarks: Set 7 Spotter 9 – Slow sand filter model

spotter.Title: Spotter 10
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the organization
spotter.Answer_Key_A: NPCDCS — National Programme for Prevention & Control of Cancer, Diabetes, Cardiovascular Diseases and Stroke, launched 2010.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State its primary objective. Mention its role in India.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Objective: prevention and control of NCDs. Role: national screening and management.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Explain its contribution to NCD control.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Provides integrated NCD services, awareness, and treatment nationwide.

spotter.Title: Spotter 11
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the scenario phases
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Haddon Matrix – Fall injury in elderly at home — phases: pre‑event, event, post‑event.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: List one host factor, one agent/vehicle factor, and one environmental factor relevant to this scenario.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Host: frailty, poor balance. Environment: unsafe flooring, poor lighting.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Propose preventive interventions for each phase.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Pre‑event: home modifications. Event: use of walking aids. Post‑event: rehabilitation and fall prevention training.
spotter.Remarks: Set 7 Spotter 11 – Haddon Matrix: Fall injury in an elderly person at home

spotter.Title: Spotter 1
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the specimen and describe two identification features
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Aedes aegypti adult — lyre-shaped white markings on the thorax and banded legs.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: 1. Name three diseases transmitted by this vector. 2. State its typical biting time.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Dengue, chikungunya, and Zika. It is a day-biting mosquito, active mainly in early morning and late afternoon.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss one community-based control strategy against this vector.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Source reduction of container breeding sites and a weekly dry day; targeted under NVBDCP.

spotter.Title: Spotter 2
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the specimen and describe how it affects the skin.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Sarcoptes scabiei (itch mite) — a microscopic mite that burrows into the skin.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State the disease it causes, and explain how it spreads within households.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Scabies; spreads through prolonged direct skin-to-skin contact, common among household or institutional contacts.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Suggest one measure to prevent outbreaks in crowded settings.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Personal hygiene and treatment of close contacts; outbreak management in institutional settings.

spotter.Title: Spotter 3
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the food item and its nutrient group.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Soybean — pulse or oilseed.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State why it is considered superior to other pulses in protein quality.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: It has the highest plant protein content among common pulses and a relatively better amino acid profile.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss its use in addressing protein-energy malnutrition.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Used in fortified food blends and school feeding programmes to improve dietary protein intake.

spotter.Title: Spotter 4
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the food item and its nutrient group.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Almonds — nut.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State one vitamin it is rich in. Explain its relevance in diets.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Rich in vitamin E, an antioxidant that helps protect cell membranes and supports skin and immune health.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss its role in a heart-healthy diet.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Its unsaturated fat content is often promoted in dietary counselling to reduce cardiovascular risk.

spotter.Title: Spotter 5
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the vaccine and state where it is used under UIP.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: JE (Japanese Encephalitis) vaccine — given in JE-endemic districts.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State its schedule and route of administration.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Given as a single dose at 9 months along with MR, with a booster at 16-24 months in endemic areas; subcutaneous or intramuscular route depending on the vaccine used.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Explain why this vaccine is not given nationwide.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: JE transmission is geographically restricted to specific endemic districts, so the vaccine is targeted rather than universal to optimize resource use.

spotter.Title: Spotter 6
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the card shown and state what it monitors.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Vaccine Vial Monitor (VVM) — monitors cumulative heat exposure of a vaccine vial.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: Explain how its colour change is interpreted.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: A progressive colour change indicates increasing heat exposure; when the inner square matches or becomes darker than the outer circle, the vaccine must be discarded regardless of expiry date.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss its significance for outreach immunization sessions.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Allows health workers to confirm vaccine potency in the field without relying solely on cold chain records, especially in remote areas.

spotter.Title: Spotter 7
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the method shown and its category.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Female condom — barrier method.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: Explain how it is inserted and state one advantage over the male condom.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Inserted into the vagina before intercourse using a flexible inner ring. Gives women more control over protection and can be inserted in advance.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss one limitation relevant to client counselling.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Higher cost and less familiarity among users compared to male condoms, requiring more detailed counselling on correct insertion.

spotter.Title: Spotter 8
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the instrument shown and the procedure it is used in.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Filshie clip — used in tubal occlusion.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State the material it is made of, and explain how it achieves occlusion.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Titanium clip lined with silicone rubber; it compresses and occludes a loop of the fallopian tube.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss one advantage of this method over ring-based occlusion.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Causes less tissue damage and is associated with a secure locking mechanism.

spotter.Title: Spotter 9
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the equipment shown and state what it measures.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: DPD chlorine comparator — measures residual chlorine in treated water.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: Explain the principle behind its colour-based reading.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: DPD reagent reacts with residual chlorine to produce a pink colour, whose intensity is compared against a standard colour scale to estimate concentration.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss its importance in monitoring water safety.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Ensures water maintains the recommended free residual chlorine level for continued protection against microbial contamination.

spotter.Title: Spotter 10
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the organization shown and state the year it was established.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: NACO — established 1992.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State its primary focus area.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Prevention and control of HIV or AIDS in India.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Explain why targeted interventions are emphasized in this programme.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: High-risk groups contribute disproportionately to transmission, so focused interventions achieve greater impact than universal approaches alone.

spotter.Title: Spotter 11
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify and tell key host and environmental factors
spotter.Sub_Question_B: Enumerate modifiable and non modifiable risk factors
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss primary, secondary, and tertiary prevention strategies for this condition.
spotter.Remarks: Set 8 Spotter 11 – Web of Causation: Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD)

spotter.Title: Spotter 1
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the specimen and describe how its siphon attaches within the water.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Mansonia larva — siphon adapted to attach to the roots of aquatic plants.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State its typical breeding habitat, and explain why this makes control difficult.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Ponds and marshes with Pistia and other aquatic plants; because the larvae attach to submerged plant roots for oxygen, larvicide alone is often ineffective without removing the vegetation.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Suggest an environmental control measure targeting this breeding site.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Removal of Pistia and other aquatic weeds; relevant programme: NVBDCP.

spotter.Title: Spotter 2
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the specimen and describe its resting wing position.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Tsetse fly (Glossina) — wings folded scissor-like at rest, with a forward-projecting proboscis.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: Name the disease it transmits, and state whether it is a concern in India.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: African trypanosomiasis (sleeping sickness); not endemic to India, included here for comparative vector study.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss control measures used where this vector is endemic.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Fly traps and clearance of bush habitat; not applicable in the Indian context.

spotter.Title: Spotter 3
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the food item and its nutrient group.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Kidney beans (Rajma) — pulse.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State one mineral it is a good source of. Explain its relevance in diets.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Good source of iron, important for preventing nutritional anaemia, especially in vegetarian diets.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss its role in a balanced vegetarian meal pattern.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Commonly combined with rice or wheat to improve overall protein quality through complementary amino acid profiles.

spotter.Title: Spotter 4
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the food item and its nutrient group.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Citrus fruit (orange or lemon) — fruit.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State one vitamin it is rich in. Explain its relevance in diets.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Rich in vitamin C, which supports immune function and enhances absorption of dietary iron.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss its relevance to a public health micronutrient strategy.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Promoted in dietary counselling as an accessible vitamin C source alongside iron-rich foods to combat anaemia.

spotter.Title: Spotter 5
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the vaccine shown and state at what ages it is given.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: DPT booster — given at 16-24 months and again at 5-6 years.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State what it protects against, and mention its route of administration.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Diphtheria, pertussis, and tetanus; given intramuscularly.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Explain why booster doses are necessary despite primary vaccination in infancy.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Immunity from primary doses wanes over time, so boosters are needed to maintain adequate protective antibody levels through childhood.

spotter.Title: Spotter 6
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the card shown and state what it detects.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Freeze indicator card (Freeze Watch) — detects accidental freezing of freeze-sensitive vaccines.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: Explain how it visually indicates freeze exposure.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: The card shows a visible change, such as a colour shift or window indicator, once the vaccine has been exposed to freezing temperatures.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss why this matters for freeze-sensitive vaccines like Pentavalent.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Freezing damages these vaccines irreversibly, reducing potency even though the vial may look and feel normal.

spotter.Title: Spotter 7
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the method shown and its category.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Combined oral contraceptive pill — hormonal method.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State the missed-pill rule for a single missed pill, and mention one non-contraceptive benefit.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Take the missed pill as soon as remembered and continue the rest as scheduled. Reduces risk of ovarian and endometrial cancer with long-term use.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss one contraindication relevant to client counselling.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Not recommended for smokers over 35 years or women with a history of thromboembolism, per WHO Medical Eligibility Criteria.

spotter.Title: Spotter 8
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the instrument set shown and the procedure it supports.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Minilap kit — instrument set for interval or postpartum female sterilization.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State the timing during which this procedure is commonly performed.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Performed either as an interval procedure or within 7 days of delivery as a postpartum procedure.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss one precaution relevant to client selection.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Requires informed consent and counselling on permanence, as the procedure is not easily reversible.

spotter.Title: Spotter 9
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the equipment shown and state its purpose.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Autoclave — used for steam sterilization of instruments or waste.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: Explain the principle by which it achieves sterilization.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Uses pressurized steam at high temperature for a set duration to kill all microorganisms, including spores.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss its significance in preventing healthcare-associated infections.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Ensures reusable instruments and certain categories of biomedical waste are rendered safe before reuse or disposal.

spotter.Title: Spotter 10
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the programme shown and state the year it was launched.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: NPCB&VI — launched in 1976 as NPCB.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State its primary objective.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Control of blindness and visual impairment in India.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Explain why cataract surgery has historically been a major focus of this programme.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Cataract is the leading cause of avoidable blindness in India, so surgical services form the backbone of the programme's impact.

spotter.Title: Spotter 11
spotter.Sub_Question_A: For this scenario, name the three phases of the Haddon Matrix.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Pre-event, event, and post-event phases.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State one host factor and one agent factor relevant to pesticide poisoning in agricultural workers.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Host: lack of protective equipment use. Agent: concentration and toxicity of the pesticide formulation.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Propose one preventive intervention for each phase.
spotter.Remarks: Set 9 Spotter 11 – Haddon Matrix: Acute pesticide poisoning in an agricultural worker

spotter.Title: Spotter 1
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the specimen and describe its wing scaling.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Mansonia adult — dark scaling on the wings and a distinctive resting posture.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: Name the disease it transmits, and state the type of filariasis involved.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Brugian filariasis, caused by Brugia malayi.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Suggest a control measure targeting its breeding association with aquatic plants.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Removal of attached aquatic vegetation; targeted under NVBDCP.

spotter.Title: Spotter 2
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the specimen and state its role in a parasite life cycle.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Lymnaea snail — spiral shell, acts as an intermediate host.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: Name the disease it transmits, and state how humans typically acquire it.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Fascioliasis (liver fluke infection); acquired by ingesting contaminated aquatic vegetation such as watercress.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss one control measure targeting this intermediate host.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Molluscicide use and drainage of snail habitats; general environmental sanitation.

spotter.Title: Spotter 3
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the food item and its nutrient group.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Egg — animal-source food.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: Explain why it is considered a reference protein.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Its amino acid composition closely matches human requirements, making it a benchmark against which other protein sources are compared.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss its role in complementary feeding for infants.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Recommended as an early complementary food due to its high-quality protein and micronutrient density.

spotter.Title: Spotter 4
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the food item and its nutrient group.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Spinach — green leafy vegetable.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State one mineral it is rich in. Explain its relevance in diets.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Rich in iron, important for preventing nutritional anaemia, though its non-heme iron is less readily absorbed than iron from animal sources.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss a counselling point to improve its iron bioavailability.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Consuming it with a vitamin C-rich food enhances iron absorption.

spotter.Title: Spotter 5
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the vaccine shown and state the two groups it is routinely given to.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: TT/Td — given to pregnant women and school-age children.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State its purpose in pregnancy, and mention its route.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Prevents neonatal and maternal tetanus by inducing passive immunity in the newborn; given intramuscularly.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Explain why tetanus toxoid remains critical despite improved institutional delivery rates.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Home deliveries and unhygienic cord care practices still occur in some areas, so maternal immunization remains an important safeguard.

spotter.Title: Spotter 6
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the label shown and state what it indicates.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Open-vial policy label — indicates which vaccines can be used in subsequent sessions after opening.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: Name one category of vaccine this policy applies to, and explain the underlying reasoning.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Multi-dose liquid vaccines like OPV that show no visible contamination and remain within cold chain can be used in later sessions, avoiding unnecessary wastage.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss its importance for reducing vaccine wastage.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Allows partially used vials to be retained under strict conditions, reducing programmatic costs while maintaining safety.

spotter.Title: Spotter 7
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the method shown and its category.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Progesterone-only pill  — hormonal method.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State one group of women for whom this is preferred over combined pills.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Preferred for lactating women and those with contraindications to estrogen, such as hypertension.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss one counselling point regarding its use.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Requires strict adherence to timing each day, as its effectiveness is more schedule-sensitive than combined pills.

spotter.Title: Spotter 8
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the instrument shown.  In which procedure is this instrument used?
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Lippie’s Loop. intrauterine contraceptive device (IUCD) for long‑term reversible contraception.
spotter.Sub_Question_B:
Explain its function during the procedure. 
Discuss one limitation in regard to modern counter part
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Higher rates of expulsion and menorrhagia were reported with Lippie’s Loop, leading to its replacement by newer IUCDs such as Copper‑T devices.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: What is one advantage
spotter.Answer_Key_C: It provides long‑term contraception without requiring daily compliance, making it more convenient and reducing user‑related failure.

spotter.Title: Spotter 9
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the equipment shown and state its purpose.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: UV germicidal lamp — used for disinfection of air, water, or surfaces.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: Explain the mechanism by which it inactivates microorganisms.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Emits ultraviolet radiation that damages microbial DNA, preventing replication and inactivating pathogens.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss one limitation of this disinfection method.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Requires direct exposure and does not leave a residual protective effect, unlike chemical disinfectants.

spotter.Title: Spotter 10
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the programme shown and What does the logo symbolize?
spotter.Answer_Key_A: National Family Planning Programme. It depicts a small, happy family,  symbolizing the ideal of family planning and population stabilization.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: Which year was India’s Family Planning Programme launched and its importance across international border?
spotter.Answer_Key_B: 1952, making India the first country in the world to adopt a national family planning programme.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss the significance of the Family Planning Programme logo in public health communication.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: The logo serves as a visual cue for awareness campaigns, reinforcing the concept of the “small family norm.” It communicates the government’s commitment to reproductive health, contraception access, and population stabilization. It also helps in community mobilization by providing a recognizable symbol across literacy levels.

spotter.Title: Spotter 11
spotter.Sub_Question_A:
Identify the diagram shown.
Name two host factors depicted in the web.
Mention one environmental factor contributing to cervical cancer.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: Explain how multiple causes interact in the web of causation for cervical cancer.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Outline prevention strategies at primary, secondary, and tertiary levels.
spotter.Remarks: Set 10 Spotter 11 – Web of Causation: Cervical Cancer

spotter.Title: Spotter 1
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the specimen and state where it typically breeds.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Anopheles adult — breeds in clean, stagnant water collections (referring to its larval habitat).
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State its public health importance in India.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Principal vector of malaria in India.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss the vector control programme relevant to this specimen.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Indoor residual spraying and insecticide-treated nets; relevant programme: NVBDCP.

spotter.Title: Spotter 2
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the specimen and describe its mouthparts.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Housefly — sponging mouthparts and four dark longitudinal stripes on the thorax.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State the diseases it transmits, and explain the mode of transmission.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Typhoid, cholera, and other diarrhoeal diseases; transmitted mechanically on its body and legs rather than through biting.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss a control measure applicable to this vector.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Proper garbage disposal and fly-proofing of food; general sanitation and food hygiene measures.

spotter.Title: Spotter 3
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the food item and its nutrient group.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Cow's milk — animal-source food.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State two nutrients it is a good source of.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Good source of protein and calcium, with lower fat content compared to buffalo milk.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss its role in a school nutrition programme.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Often included in mid-day meal or supplementary nutrition schemes to improve protein and calcium intake in children.

spotter.Title: Spotter 4
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the item shown and state its major harmful constituent.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Alcohol — ethanol.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State its principal health effects, and mention the population group most at risk.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Liver cirrhosis, dependence, and road traffic accidents; adults, particularly heavy or binge drinkers, are most at risk.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss the regulatory approach to controlling alcohol-related harm.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: State excise regulation and the WHO SAFER framework for alcohol control.

spotter.Title: Spotter 5
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the vaccine shown and state when it must be given.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Hepatitis B birth dose — given within 24 hours of birth.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: Explain why timing is so critical for this vaccine.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Early administration prevents mother-to-child transmission of Hepatitis B, which carries a high risk of chronic infection if acquired at birth.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss a programmatic challenge in achieving high birth dose coverage.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Requires availability of the vaccine at every delivery point, including home deliveries, which remains a logistical challenge in some areas.

spotter.Title: Spotter 6
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the equipment shown and state its purpose.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Hub-cutter — used to safely destroy used needles and syringes.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: Explain how it contributes to safe waste management.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Separates and destroys the needle hub immediately after use, preventing needle-stick injury and unauthorized reuse of syringes.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss its role within biomedical waste management guidelines.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: An essential step in point-of-use segregation and safe disposal of sharps under biomedical waste management rules.

spotter.Title: Spotter 7
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the method shown and its category.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Contraceptive implant — hormonal method.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State how long it provides protection, and mention where it is placed.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Provides protection for several years; a subdermal rod inserted under the skin of the upper arm.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss one counselling point relevant to its removal.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Must be removed by a trained provider before or at the end of its effective duration, and fertility returns quickly after removal.

spotter.Title: Spotter 8
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the instrument shown and the procedure it supports.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Laparoscope — used for laparoscopic tubal ligation.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: Explain the advantage of this approach over open surgery.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Allows visualization and tubal occlusion through small incisions, reducing recovery time and scarring compared to open surgery.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss one precaution required for its safe use.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Requires trained personnel and appropriate anaesthesia facilities, as it involves abdominal entry and gas insufflation.

spotter.Title: Spotter 9
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the equipment shown and state its purpose.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: N95 respirator — personal protective equipment against airborne particulates or pathogens.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: Explain what the number in its name signifies.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Indicates that it filters at least 95 percent of airborne particles when properly fitted.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss its significance in preventing occupational and airborne infections.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Critical protective equipment for healthcare workers managing airborne diseases such as tuberculosis or during respiratory disease outbreaks.

spotter.Title: Spotter 10
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the programme shown and state the year it was launched.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Poshan Abhiyaan — launched in 2018.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State its primary objective.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Reduction of stunting, undernutrition, and anaemia among children, adolescents, and women.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Explain why a convergence approach was adopted for this programme.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Malnutrition has multiple causes spanning health, sanitation, and food security, requiring coordination across multiple ministries and schemes.

spotter.Title: Spotter 11
spotter.Sub_Question_A: For this scenario, name the three phases of the Haddon Matrix.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Pre-event, event, and post-event phases.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State one host factor and one agent factor relevant to workplace machinery injury.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Host: inadequate training or fatigue. Agent: absence of machine safety guards.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Propose one preventive intervention for each phase.
spotter.Remarks: Set 11 Spotter 11 – Haddon Matrix: Workplace machinery entanglement injury

spotter.Title: Spotter 1
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the specimen and state its typical breeding site.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Culex adult — breeds in polluted or stagnant water and drains.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State the diseases it is associated with.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Lymphatic filariasis and Japanese encephalitis.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss the control programme targeting this vector.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Source reduction of polluted water bodies; relevant programme: NVBDCP.

spotter.Title: Spotter 2
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the specimen and describe a distinguishing feature of its mouth structure.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Hookworm — small, greyish-white worm with a buccal cavity bearing teeth or cutting plates.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State the disease it causes, and explain how infection occurs.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Hookworm infection, a leading cause of iron-deficiency anaemia; occurs through skin penetration from contaminated soil, typically through bare feet.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss one preventive measure promoted under the national deworming programme.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Footwear use, deworming, and safe excreta disposal; National Deworming Day.

spotter.Title: Spotter 3
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the food item and its nutrient group.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Buffalo milk — animal-source food.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State how it differs from cow's milk in composition.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Has a higher fat content compared to cow's milk.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss a dietary consideration relevant to its higher fat content.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: May require moderation in individuals managing weight or cardiovascular risk factors.

spotter.Title: Spotter 4
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the item shown and state its major harmful constituents.
