spotter.Answer_Key_A: Cigarette — nicotine, tar, and carcinogens.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State its principal health effects, and mention the population group most at risk.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: COPD, lung cancer, and cardiovascular disease; smokers and passive smokers are both at risk.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss the legislative framework addressing tobacco use in India.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: National Tobacco Control Programme and the Cigarettes and Other Tobacco Products Act (COTPA) 2003.

spotter.Title: Spotter 5
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the vaccine shown and state the programme under which it was administered.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: COVID-19 vaccine — administered under the national COVID vaccination programme.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State one platform used for COVID-19 vaccines in India.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Both inactivated whole-virion and viral vector platforms were used in India's vaccination programme.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss a key lesson for immunization systems learned from this rollout.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Highlighted the importance of digital registration and tracking systems, later adapted into platforms like CoWIN and U-WIN.

spotter.Title: Spotter 6
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the item shown and state its purpose.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Biomedical waste bag — used for safe disposal of used vaccine vials and syringes.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: Explain the colour-coding principle behind such bags.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Different colours correspond to different waste categories and required treatment methods, ensuring correct segregation at the point of generation.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss its importance in an immunization session.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Prevents needle-stick injuries and environmental contamination from improperly discarded sharps and vials.

spotter.Title: Spotter 7
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the method shown and its category.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Diaphragm — barrier method.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: Explain how it is used, and mention what it should be combined with for effectiveness.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: A dome-shaped device inserted into the vagina to cover the cervix before intercourse; should be used with spermicide for better effectiveness.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss one limitation relevant to client counselling.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Requires correct fitting by a trained provider and consistent use with every act of intercourse.

spotter.Title: Spotter 8
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the method shown and its category.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Contraceptive patch — hormonal method.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State how frequently it is changed, and mention its route of hormone delivery.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Changed weekly; delivers hormones transdermally through the skin.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss one counselling point relevant to its use.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Must be applied to clean, dry skin and checked regularly to ensure it remains firmly attached.

spotter.Title: Spotter 9
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the equipment shown and state its purpose.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: PPE kit — comprehensive personal protective equipment set.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: Name the components typically included in such a kit.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Gown, gloves, mask, eye protection, and head cover, depending on the level of protection required.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss its significance in occupational and infection control settings.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Protects healthcare and sanitation workers from exposure to infectious or hazardous materials during patient care or waste handling.

spotter.Title: Spotter 10
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the scheme shown and state the year it was launched.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Janani Suraksha Yojana (JSY) — launched in 2005.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State its primary objective.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Promotion of institutional delivery to reduce maternal and neonatal mortality.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Explain the mechanism by which it incentivizes institutional delivery.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Provides cash assistance to pregnant women who deliver in a government or accredited private health facility.

spotter.Title: Spotter 11
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the key host and environmental factors contributing to Essential Hypertension.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: Construct a web of causation linking these factors to the disease.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss prevention strategies at each level for this condition.
spotter.Remarks: Set 12 Spotter 11 – Web of Causation: Essential Hypertension

spotter.Title: Spotter 1
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the specimen and state its typical breeding site.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Aedes adult — breeds in clean water in containers, tyres, and coolers.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State the diseases associated with this specimen.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Dengue, chikungunya, and Zika.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss the vector control programme relevant to this specimen.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Source reduction of container breeding sites and a weekly dry day; relevant programme: NVBDCP.

spotter.Title: Spotter 2
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the specimen and describe its shape.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Fasciola hepatica — a flat, leaf-shaped fluke.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State the disease it causes, and explain how humans become infected.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Fascioliasis (liver fluke infection); acquired through ingestion of contaminated aquatic vegetation, via a snail intermediate host.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss one preventive measure relevant to this infection.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Avoiding raw aquatic vegetation and controlling the snail intermediate host; veterinary and environmental sanitation measures.

spotter.Title: Spotter 3
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the food item and its nutrient group.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Paneer — milk product.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State what it is a concentrated source of.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: A concentrated source of milk protein.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss its relevance for vegetarian populations.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: An important protein source for lacto-vegetarian diets that exclude meat, fish, and eggs.

spotter.Title: Spotter 4
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the item shown and state its major harmful constituents.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Tobacco pouch (chewing tobacco or gutka) — nicotine, areca nut, and carcinogens.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State its principal health effects, and mention the population group most at risk.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Oral cancer and oral submucous fibrosis; smokeless tobacco users, including adolescents, are at particular risk.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss the regulatory measures addressing this product in India.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: National Tobacco Control Programme, COTPA 2003, and the gutka or pan masala ban under FSSAI.

spotter.Title: Spotter 5
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the vaccine shown and state its advantage over older typhoid vaccines.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Typhoid conjugate vaccine — provides longer-lasting protection than older typhoid vaccines.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State the age group it can be given to.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Can be given to infants from 6 months of age, unlike earlier polysaccharide vaccines.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss why conjugate technology improves vaccine performance in young children.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Conjugation to a carrier protein produces a stronger immune response in infants, whose immune systems respond poorly to plain polysaccharide antigens.

spotter.Title: Spotter 6
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the equipment shown and state its purpose.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Deep freezer — used to freeze ice packs at the cold chain point.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: Explain why this equipment is kept separate from vaccine storage refrigerators.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Vaccines must never be exposed to freezing temperatures, so ice packs are frozen in a dedicated deep freezer rather than alongside vaccines.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss its role in supporting outreach immunization sessions.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Ensures a continuous supply of frozen ice packs needed to maintain cold chain temperature in vaccine carriers during transport.

spotter.Title: Spotter 7
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the method shown and its category.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Cervical cap — barrier method.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: Explain how it differs in fit from a diaphragm.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: It is smaller and fits snugly over the cervix itself by suction, rather than spanning the entire vaginal vault like a diaphragm.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss one limitation relevant to client counselling.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Requires correct fitting and is generally less effective in women who have previously given birth.

spotter.Title: Spotter 8
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the method shown and its category.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Vaginal ring — hormonal method.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State how it is used, and mention its duration of action.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Self-inserted into the vagina and left in place; typically used for three weeks followed by a ring-free week each cycle.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss one counselling point relevant to its use.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Requires the woman to be comfortable with vaginal self-insertion and removal, and to follow the correct in-use schedule.

spotter.Title: Spotter 9
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the equipment shown and state its purpose.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Noise dosimeter — used to measure occupational noise exposure.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: Explain how it is typically used in a workplace assessment.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Worn by a worker over a shift to record cumulative noise exposure, which is then compared against permissible exposure limits.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss its significance in preventing occupational hearing loss.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Identifies workers at risk of noise-induced hearing loss, guiding decisions on hearing protection and engineering controls.

spotter.Title: Spotter 10
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the scheme shown and state the year it was launched.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: PMSMA — launched in 2016.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State what service it guarantees, and on which day.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Free antenatal check-ups for pregnant women on the 9th of every month.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Explain why a fixed monthly day approach was chosen for this scheme.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: A predictable, fixed date helps mobilize both specialist volunteers and pregnant women, improving turnout and quality of check-ups.

spotter.Title: Spotter 11
spotter.Sub_Question_A: For this scenario, name the three phases of the Haddon Matrix.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Pre-event, event, and post-event phases.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State one host factor and one environmental factor relevant to dog bite injury in a rural child.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Host: unsupervised young child. Environment: presence of free-roaming unvaccinated dogs.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Propose one preventive intervention for each phase.
spotter.Remarks: Set 13 Spotter 11 – Haddon Matrix: Dog bite injury in a child in a rural setting

spotter.Title: Spotter 1
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the specimen and describe its appearance.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Housefly egg — tiny, white, oval eggs laid in batches on decaying organic matter.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State its typical breeding habitat.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Decaying organic matter and animal excreta.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss the public health importance of this stage and its relevance to control measures.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Proper garbage disposal and fly-proofing of food; general sanitation and food hygiene measures.

spotter.Title: Spotter 2
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the specimen and describe its body form.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Sandfly larva — caterpillar-like body with bristles.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State its typical breeding habitat.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Cracks in walls, rubble, and moist organic matter.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss the relevance of this stage to the vector control programme.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Indoor residual spraying and treatment of cracks or crevices; National Kala-azar Elimination Programme.

spotter.Title: Spotter 3
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the food item and its nutrient group.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Fish — animal-source food.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State two nutrients it is a good source of.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Good quality protein and omega-3 fatty acids.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss its relevance to cardiovascular health in dietary counselling.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Omega-3 fatty acids are often promoted for their protective role against cardiovascular disease.

spotter.Title: Spotter 4
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the item shown and state its major harmful constituents.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Energy drink — high caffeine and sugar content.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State its principal health effects, and mention the population group most at risk.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Cardiac arrhythmia, insomnia, and obesity risk; adolescents and young adults are most at risk.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss the regulatory approach addressing this product.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: FSSAI caffeine-labelling regulations and school nutrition guidelines.

spotter.Title: Spotter 5
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the vaccine shown and state when it is given.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Anti-rabies vaccine (ARV) — given as post-exposure prophylaxis after animal bites.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State its schedule, and mention the exposure category it is used for.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Given on days 0, 3, 7, and 28 in the standard intramuscular regimen; used for Category II and III exposures.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss why timely administration after a bite is critical.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Rabies is almost universally fatal once symptoms appear, so prompt post-exposure prophylaxis is essential to prevent disease onset.

spotter.Title: Spotter 6
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the item shown and state its purpose.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Dry ice pack — alternative cold chain material for specific vaccine transport.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: Explain how it differs from a standard water-based ice pack.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Dry ice maintains much colder temperatures through sublimation and is used for vaccines or specimens requiring ultra-cold transport conditions.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss a precaution needed when using this material.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Requires careful handling and ventilation, as it can cause cold burns and releases carbon dioxide gas.

spotter.Title: Spotter 7
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the method shown and its category.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Spermicide — chemical barrier method.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: Explain how it works, and mention how it is typically combined with other methods.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Contains a chemical agent that inactivates or kills sperm; often used together with a barrier method such as a condom or diaphragm for better effectiveness.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss one limitation relevant to client counselling.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Has a relatively high failure rate when used alone, so it should be recommended primarily as an adjunct method.

spotter.Title: Spotter 8
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the kit shown and state its purpose.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: IUCD insertion kit — full instrument set for IUCD insertion.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: Name one instrument typically included in this kit.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Uterine sound, used to measure the depth and direction of the uterine cavity before insertion.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss why using a complete sterile kit matters for this procedure.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Reduces the risk of infection and ensures correct technique during insertion.

spotter.Title: Spotter 9
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the equipment shown and state its purpose.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Lux meter — used to measure workplace illumination levels.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: Explain why illumination assessment matters in occupational settings.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Inadequate lighting can contribute to eye strain, reduced productivity, and increased risk of workplace accidents.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss its relevance to occupational health standards.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Used to verify that workplace lighting meets recommended standards for the type of task being performed.

spotter.Title: Spotter 10
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the scheme shown and state the year it was launched.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Ayushman Bharat or PMJAY — launched in 2018.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State its primary objective.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Health insurance coverage for economically vulnerable families.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Explain why this scheme is considered significant for reducing catastrophic health expenditure.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Provides cashless hospitalization coverage, protecting low-income families from being pushed into poverty due to high medical costs.

spotter.Title: Spotter 11
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the key host and environmental factors contributing to Stroke.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: Construct a web of causation linking these factors to the disease.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss prevention strategies at each level for this condition.
spotter.Remarks: Set 14 Spotter 11 – Web of Causation: Stroke

spotter.Title: Spotter 1
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the specimen and describe its appearance.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Housefly larva (maggot) — a legless, whitish maggot.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State its typical breeding habitat.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Decaying organic matter and animal excreta.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss the relevance of this stage to control measures.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Proper garbage disposal and fly-proofing of food; general sanitation and food hygiene measures.

spotter.Title: Spotter 2
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the specimen and describe where it is typically laid.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Sandfly egg — small eggs laid singly in cracks and moist organic matter.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State its typical breeding habitat.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Cracks in walls, rubble, and moist organic matter.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss the relevance of this stage to the vector control programme.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Indoor residual spraying and treatment of cracks or crevices; National Kala-azar Elimination Programme.

spotter.Title: Spotter 3
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the food item and its nutrient group.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Chicken or meat — animal-source food.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State what quality of protein it provides.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Good quality animal protein source with a complete amino acid profile.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss a food safety consideration relevant to its consumption.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Requires adequate cooking temperatures to prevent foodborne illness from bacterial contamination.

spotter.Title: Spotter 4
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the food item and its nutrient group.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Honey — sweetener.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State one precaution relevant to feeding this to infants.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Should not be given to infants under one year due to the risk of infant botulism.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss its use in nutrition counselling for adults.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Sometimes suggested as a natural alternative to refined sugar, though it should still be consumed in moderation.

spotter.Title: Spotter 5
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the item shown and state when it is used.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Anti-snake venom (ASV) — used in management of venomous snakebite.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State its route of administration, and mention what it is derived from.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Given intravenously; derived from antibodies raised in horses or sheep against venom from specific snake species.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss a precaution needed before its administration.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Patients should be observed for anaphylactic or serum reactions, and facilities for managing such reactions should be available.

spotter.Title: Spotter 6
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the equipment shown and state the temperature range it maintains.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Ice-Lined Refrigerator (ILR) — maintains +2 degrees Celsius to +8 degrees Celsius.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: Explain how its ice-lining feature helps during power outages.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: The ice lining absorbs and releases cold gradually, helping maintain safe temperatures for several hours even without continuous electricity.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss its role at the primary health centre cold chain point.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Serves as the main vaccine storage unit at the facility level, from which vaccines are drawn for outreach sessions.

spotter.Title: Spotter 7
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the item shown and the method it supports.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Standard Days Method (SDM) beads — fertility awareness method.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: Explain how the beads are used to track the cycle.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Each bead represents a day of the menstrual cycle, colour-coded to indicate fertile and infertile days, helping the couple avoid unprotected intercourse on fertile days.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss one limitation relevant to client counselling.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Only suitable for women with regular menstrual cycles of a specific length range.

spotter.Title: Spotter 8
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the instrument shown and its purpose.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Cu-T removal hook — used for IUCD removal.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: Explain the technique used with this instrument.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: The hook is used to gently grasp and withdraw the IUCD threads or device from the uterine cavity.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss one precaution during removal.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Should be performed by a trained provider to avoid trauma or incomplete removal of the device.

spotter.Title: Spotter 9
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the equipment shown and state its purpose.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Spirometer — used to assess occupational lung function, such as in silicosis screening.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: Explain what parameters it typically measures.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Measures lung volumes and airflow rates, such as forced vital capacity and forced expiratory volume.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss its relevance in monitoring workers exposed to dust hazards.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Detects early restrictive or obstructive lung changes in workers exposed to silica or other occupational dusts, enabling early intervention.

spotter.Title: Spotter 10
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the mission shown and state the year it was launched.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Swachh Bharat Mission — launched in 2014.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State its primary objective.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Achieving universal sanitation coverage and an open-defecation-free status.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Explain the public health rationale behind this mission.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Reducing open defecation lowers faeco-oral disease transmission, directly impacting diarrhoeal disease and child health outcomes.

spotter.Title: Spotter 11
spotter.Sub_Question_A: For this scenario, name the three phases of the Haddon Matrix.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Pre-event, event, and post-event phases.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State one host factor and one environmental factor relevant to accidental kerosene ingestion in a toddler.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Host: young child's tendency to explore by mouth. Environment: kerosene stored in an unlabelled drinking bottle within reach.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Propose one preventive intervention for each phase.
spotter.Remarks: Set 15 Spotter 11 – Haddon Matrix: Accidental kerosene ingestion in a toddler

spotter.Title: Spotter 1
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the specimen and describe the appearance of its shell.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Ascaris egg — thick, mammillated (bumpy), bile-stained oval shell.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State the disease it causes, and explain how humans become infected.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Ascariasis; humans are infected through the faeco-oral route via soil-contaminated food or hands.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss the national programme addressing this infection in India.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Deworming, safe excreta disposal, hand hygiene; National Deworming Day.

spotter.Title: Spotter 2
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the specimen and state its typical breeding habitat.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Sandfly — breeds in cracks in walls, rubble, and moist organic matter.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State the diseases associated with this specimen.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Visceral leishmaniasis (kala-azar) and oriental sore.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss the vector control programme relevant to this specimen.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Indoor residual spraying and treatment of cracks or crevices; National Kala-azar Elimination Programme.

spotter.Title: Spotter 3
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the food item and its nutrient group.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Carrot — root vegetable.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State one vitamin precursor it is rich in. Explain its relevance in diets.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Rich in beta-carotene, a precursor of vitamin A important for vision and immune function.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss its relevance to a public health micronutrient programme.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Promoted in dietary counselling as a low-cost source to help prevent vitamin A deficiency and related eye disorders.

spotter.Title: Spotter 4
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the food item and its nutrient group.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Refined sugar — sweetener.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: Explain why it is described as a source of empty calories.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Provides energy without any accompanying vitamins, minerals, or fibre.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss a dietary counselling message relevant to its consumption.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Advised to be consumed in moderation to reduce risk of obesity, dental caries, and non-communicable diseases.

spotter.Title: Spotter 5
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the vaccine shown and state the three diseases it protects against.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: MMR — measles, mumps, and rubella.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State its schedule, and mention its route.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Given as part of the two-dose measles-rubella schedule under UIP; subcutaneous route.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss why combination vaccines like this are programmatically preferred.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Reduces the number of injections and visits required, improving coverage and compliance compared to separate single-antigen vaccines.

spotter.Title: Spotter 6
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the device shown and state its purpose.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: 30-DTR (Day Temperature Recorder) device — used to continuously monitor vaccine storage temperature.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: Explain what advantage it offers over manual twice-daily temperature checks.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Provides continuous automated recording, capturing temperature excursions that might be missed between manual checks.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss its significance for cold chain quality assurance.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Provides objective evidence of storage conditions, supporting accountability and early identification of cold chain equipment failure.

spotter.Title: Spotter 7
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the method shown and its category.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Basal Body Temperature (BBT) method — fertility awareness method.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: Explain the physiological basis of this method.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Body temperature rises slightly after ovulation due to increased progesterone, allowing the fertile window to be identified retrospectively.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss one limitation relevant to client counselling.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Temperature can be affected by illness, poor sleep, or environmental factors, reducing reliability if not measured consistently.

spotter.Title: Spotter 8
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the instrument shown and its purpose.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: PPIUCD inserter — used for postpartum IUCD insertion.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State the timing during which it is typically used.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Used within 48 hours of delivery for postpartum IUCD insertion.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss one precaution relevant to its use.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Requires correct technique to reduce the risk of expulsion, which is higher in the immediate postpartum period.

spotter.Title: Spotter 9
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the equipment shown and state its purpose.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Audiometer — used to screen for noise-induced hearing loss.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: Explain how a hearing test using this equipment is conducted.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: The worker listens to tones at varying frequencies and volumes through headphones, and the softest audible sound at each frequency is recorded.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss its relevance in occupational health surveillance.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Used for baseline and periodic screening of workers in high-noise industries to detect early hearing loss.

spotter.Title: Spotter 10
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the health facility shown and state the population it is designed to serve.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Health and Wellness Centre (Ayushman Arogya Mandir) — serves the local community under comprehensive primary health care.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State the key services provided at this facility.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Provides an expanded range of services including NCD screening, maternal and child health, and mental health care, beyond the traditional Sub-Centre package.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss its role within the broader health system.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Acts as the first point of contact for comprehensive primary care, referring complex cases upward to PHCs or CHCs.

spotter.Title: Spotter 11
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the key host and environmental factors contributing to Pulmonary Tuberculosis.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: Construct a web of causation linking these factors to the disease.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss prevention strategies at each level for this condition.
spotter.Remarks: Set 16 Spotter 11 – Web of Causation: Pulmonary Tuberculosis

spotter.Title: Spotter 1
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the specimen and state its typical breeding habitat.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Housefly — breeds in decaying organic matter and animal excreta.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State the diseases associated with this specimen.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Typhoid, cholera, and other diarrhoeal diseases, transmitted mechanically.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss the control measures relevant to this specimen.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Proper garbage disposal and fly-proofing of food; general sanitation and food hygiene measures.

spotter.Title: Spotter 2
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the specimen and describe its resting wing position.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Sandfly — small, hairy body with a hopping flight, wings held in a V shape at rest.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State the diseases associated with this specimen.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Visceral leishmaniasis (kala-azar) and oriental sore.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss a control measure applicable to this vector.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Indoor residual spraying and treatment of cracks or crevices; targeted under the National Kala-azar Elimination Programme.

spotter.Title: Spotter 3
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the food item and its nutrient group.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Pumpkin — vegetable.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State one vitamin precursor it is a source of. Explain its relevance in diets.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Source of beta-carotene, important for maintaining healthy vision and immune function.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss its relevance to a public health micronutrient strategy.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Included in dietary counselling as an accessible source to help address vitamin A deficiency.

spotter.Title: Spotter 4
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the food item and its nutrient group.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Mustard oil — fat or cooking oil.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State one region where it is commonly used, and mention a dietary consideration relevant to it.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Commonly used in North India; contains erucic acid, a consideration in some dietary guidelines regarding cardiovascular health.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss its role compared to fortified oils in a public health context.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Unlike fortified edible oils, it is not typically used as a vehicle for micronutrient fortification programmes.

spotter.Title: Spotter 5
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the vaccine shown and state the disease it prevents.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Varicella vaccine — protects against chickenpox.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State its typical schedule.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Usually given as two doses in early childhood, though its inclusion varies by state and is not universally part of UIP.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss why this vaccine is not yet part of the universal schedule in India.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Chickenpox is generally a mild self-limiting illness in most children, so cost-effectiveness considerations have kept it outside the free universal schedule so far.

spotter.Title: Spotter 6
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the item shown and state the age group it is given to.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Vitamin A supplementation bottle — given to children 9 months to 5 years.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State how frequently it is administered.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Given biannually as part of routine supplementation.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss the public health rationale for this supplementation programme.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Prevents vitamin A deficiency, a leading preventable cause of childhood blindness, and reduces overall child mortality risk.

spotter.Title: Spotter 7
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the method shown and its category.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Saheli (Centchroman) — hormonal method.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State its dosing schedule, and mention what makes it distinct from standard hormonal pills.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Taken once a week after an initial loading phase; it is a non-steroidal hormonal pill, distinct from typical steroid-based oral contraceptives.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss one counselling point relevant to its use.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Requires strict adherence to its once-weekly schedule for effectiveness.

spotter.Title: Spotter 8
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the card shown and the method it supports.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Antara card — supports DMPA injectable contraception.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State what information it helps track.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Tracks the client's injection dates and due dates for follow-up doses.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss why follow-up tracking matters for this method.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Missing the follow-up window can result in loss of contraceptive protection, so tracking supports programme continuity.

spotter.Title: Spotter 9
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the equipment shown and state its purpose.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Silica dust respirator — protective equipment against silicosis-causing dust.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: Explain why standard cloth masks are inadequate for this purpose.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Silica particles are extremely fine and require a respirator with appropriate filtration efficiency, which ordinary cloth masks cannot provide.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss its relevance in preventing an irreversible occupational lung disease.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Silicosis has no cure once established, making respiratory protection a critical primary prevention measure for exposed workers.

spotter.Title: Spotter 10
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the health facility shown and state the population it is designed to serve.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Primary Health Centre (PHC) — first point of contact with a medical officer for a rural population.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State the staffing and service norms typically expected at this facility.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Staffed by a medical officer along with paramedical staff, providing outpatient care, basic emergency services, and referral linkages as per IPHS norms.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss its referral role within the health system.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Refers complex cases to the Community Health Centre or district hospital, forming a key link in the rural referral chain.

spotter.Title: Spotter 11
spotter.Sub_Question_A: For this scenario, name the three phases of the Haddon Matrix.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Pre-event, event, and post-event phases.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State one host factor and one agent factor relevant to sports-related injury in a school athlete.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Host: inadequate warm-up or conditioning. Agent: improper sports equipment or playing surface.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Propose one preventive intervention for each phase.
spotter.Remarks: Set 17 Spotter 11 – Haddon Matrix: Sports-related musculoskeletal injury in a school athlete

spotter.Title: Spotter 1
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the specimen and describe a distinguishing feature of its posterior end.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Ascaris adult male — smaller than the female, with a curved posterior end.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State the disease it causes, and mention how it is transmitted.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Ascariasis; transmitted through the faeco-oral route via soil-contaminated food or hands.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss the national programme addressing this infection.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Deworming, safe excreta disposal, hand hygiene; National Deworming Day.

spotter.Title: Spotter 2
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the specimen and describe its shell.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Tapeworm egg — round egg with a thick, radially striated shell.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State the disease it causes, and mention how humans become infected.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Taeniasis; acquired through ingestion of undercooked pork or beef containing cysticerci.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss a preventive measure relevant to this infection.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Meat inspection and thorough cooking; food safety and meat inspection regulations.

spotter.Title: Spotter 3
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the food item and its nutrient group.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Potato — root vegetable or tuber.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State what it is primarily a source of.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Primarily an energy source, with some vitamin C content.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss a consideration relevant to its preparation in nutrition counselling.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Preparation method matters, as frying significantly increases its calorie and fat content compared to boiling or baking.

spotter.Title: Spotter 4
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the food item and its category.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Fortified edible oil — fortified food.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State which vitamins it is typically fortified with.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Fortified with vitamin A and vitamin D.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss its role in a national fortification strategy.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Used as a food vehicle to address widespread vitamin A and D deficiency at the population level, since oil is consumed by nearly all households.

spotter.Title: Spotter 5
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the vaccine shown and state what it protects against.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: HPV vaccine — protects against cervical cancer-causing HPV strains.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State the age group it is recommended for, and mention its schedule.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Recommended for adolescent girls, typically given as a two-dose schedule if started before age 15.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss why early adolescent vaccination is emphasized for this vaccine.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: The vaccine is most effective when given before the onset of sexual activity and potential HPV exposure.

spotter.Title: Spotter 6
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the item shown and state its purpose.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: BCG reconstitution syringe — specific syringe used for reconstituting BCG vaccine.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: Explain why a dedicated syringe is used for this purpose.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: BCG requires precise, low-volume reconstitution with its specific diluent, and using a dedicated syringe reduces dosing errors and cross-contamination.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss a related safety practice at immunization sessions.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Reconstituted BCG vaccine must be discarded after a limited time window due to the risk of bacterial contamination once mixed.

spotter.Title: Spotter 7
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the device shown and its category.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Multiload IUCD — intrauterine device.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: Explain how its design differs from the Cu-T.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: It has a different frame shape, offered as an alternative IUCD design intended to reduce expulsion in some users.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss one counselling point common to all IUCDs.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Clients should be taught to check the device threads periodically to confirm the device remains correctly positioned.

spotter.Title: Spotter 8
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the tool shown and its purpose.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Injectable calendar — used to track follow-up dosing schedule.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: Explain why tracking matters for injectable contraceptives.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Missing the follow-up injection window can result in loss of contraceptive protection, so the calendar helps both client and provider stay on schedule.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss how this tool supports programme continuity.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Reduces discontinuation rates by prompting timely follow-up visits.

spotter.Title: Spotter 9
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the item shown and state its purpose.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Blood lead level test card — used in occupational lead exposure screening.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: Name an occupational group that would be screened using this test.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Workers in battery manufacturing, lead smelting, or paint industries are commonly screened.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss the health rationale for such screening.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Chronic lead exposure can cause neurological, renal, and haematological damage, making early detection important for occupational health surveillance.
spotter.Remarks: Set 18 Spotter 9 – Blood lead level test card

spotter.Title: Spotter 10
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the health facility shown and state the population it is designed to serve.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Community Health Centre (CHC) — serves as the first referral unit with specialist services.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State the specialist services typically available here.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Provides specialist care in medicine, surgery, obstetrics and gynaecology, and paediatrics, along with 24-hour emergency services.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss its referral relationship with PHCs and district hospitals.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Receives referrals from PHCs and refers complex cases onward to the district hospital, forming the middle tier of the rural referral system.

spotter.Title: Spotter 11
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the key host and environmental factors contributing to Childhood Stunting or Undernutrition.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: Construct a web of causation linking these factors to the condition.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss prevention strategies at each level for this condition.
spotter.Remarks: Set 18 Spotter 11 – Web of Causation: Childhood Stunting/Undernutrition

spotter.Title: Spotter 1
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the specimen and describe a distinguishing feature of its posterior end.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Ascaris adult female — larger than the male, with a straight posterior end.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State the disease it causes, and mention a complication of heavy infection.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Ascariasis; heavy infection can cause intestinal obstruction, particularly in children.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss the national programme addressing this infection.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Deworming, safe excreta disposal, hand hygiene; National Deworming Day.

spotter.Title: Spotter 2
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the specimen and describe its body structure.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Tapeworm adult (Taenia) — flat, ribbon-like, segmented body with a scolex bearing hooks or suckers.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State the disease it causes, and mention a more severe related condition.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Taeniasis; its larval form can cause cysticercosis, a more severe condition.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss a preventive measure relevant to this infection.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Meat inspection and thorough cooking; food safety and meat inspection regulations.

spotter.Title: Spotter 3
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the food item and its nutrient group.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Banana — fruit.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State one mineral it is a good source of.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Good source of potassium, along with being an energy-dense fruit.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss its relevance in a nutrition counselling context.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Often recommended as a quick energy source and for maintaining electrolyte balance, including in diarrhoea management.

spotter.Title: Spotter 4
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the item shown and its category.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: RUTF (Ready-to-Use Therapeutic Food) — therapeutic food.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State the condition it is used to manage.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Used in the management of severe acute malnutrition.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss why it is preferred over traditional therapeutic milk formulas in community settings.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Does not require water or refrigeration for preparation, making it safer and more practical for home-based management of severe acute malnutrition.

spotter.Title: Spotter 5
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the vaccine shown and state how often it is recommended.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Influenza vaccine — recommended annually for high-risk groups.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: Name one high-risk group for whom it is recommended.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Pregnant women, elderly individuals, and those with chronic illness are commonly prioritized.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss why this vaccine requires annual re-administration.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Influenza viruses undergo frequent antigenic changes, so the vaccine composition is updated each year to match circulating strains.

spotter.Title: Spotter 6
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the item shown and state its purpose.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Diluent vial — used to reconstitute freeze-dried vaccines like BCG and Measles.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: Explain why a vaccine-specific diluent must always be used.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Using the wrong diluent can inactivate the vaccine or cause serious adverse events, so each freeze-dried vaccine must only be reconstituted with its manufacturer-matched diluent.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss a related cold chain practice for diluents.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Diluents should be kept at the same temperature as their corresponding vaccine before mixing, to avoid thermal shock to the reconstituted product.

spotter.Title: Spotter 7
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the method shown and its category.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Vaginal sponge — barrier method.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: Explain how it works, and mention its duration of protection.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: A single-use sponge containing spermicide, inserted before intercourse and providing protection for repeated acts of intercourse within 24 hours.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss one limitation relevant to client counselling.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Less effective in women who have previously given birth, and does not protect against sexually transmitted infections.

spotter.Title: Spotter 8
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the card shown and its purpose.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Emergency contraception counselling card — used for client counselling on emergency contraception use and limitations.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State the key message it typically conveys about timing.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Emphasizes that emergency contraception should be taken as soon as possible after unprotected intercourse, and is not intended for regular use.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss why counselling on its limitations matters.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Helps prevent over-reliance on emergency contraception in place of a regular, more effective ongoing method.

spotter.Title: Spotter 9
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the equipment shown and state its purpose.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Fire extinguisher types — used based on the type of workplace fire hazard.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: Name the classes of fire extinguishers and what each is suited for.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Class A for ordinary combustibles, Class B for flammable liquids, Class C for electrical fires, and Class D for combustible metals.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss why correct extinguisher selection matters in a workplace.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Using the wrong type of extinguisher on certain fires, such as water on an electrical fire, can worsen the hazard rather than control it.

spotter.Title: Spotter 10
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the health facility shown and state who typically staffs it.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Sub-Centre — most peripheral contact point, typically staffed by an ANM or CHO.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State the population it is designed to serve.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Serves as the first point of contact for a defined rural population, typically covering a few thousand people.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss its role in the broader referral chain.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Provides basic preventive and promotive care and refers cases needing further management to the PHC.

spotter.Title: Spotter 11
spotter.Sub_Question_A: For this scenario, name the three phases of the Haddon Matrix.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Pre-event, event, and post-event phases.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State one host factor and one environmental factor relevant to a construction site fall from height.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Host: inadequate safety training. Environment: absence of guardrails or fall-arrest systems.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Propose one preventive intervention for each phase.
spotter.Remarks: Set 19 Spotter 11 – Haddon Matrix: Occupational fall from height at a construction site

spotter.Title: Spotter 1
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the specimen and state its role in disease transmission.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Cyclops — a small freshwater crustacean acting as an intermediate host for a parasitic nematode.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: Name the disease for which it serves as intermediate host.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Guinea worm disease (dracunculiasis), caused by Dracunculus medinensis.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss India's current status regarding this disease.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: India was certified Guinea worm-free by WHO in 2000, following a successful eradication programme.

spotter.Title: Spotter 2
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the specimen and state its public health significance.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Rat — a rodent that acts as a reservoir host and pest of public health importance.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: List diseases associated with rodents.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Plague, leptospirosis, rat-bite fever, and murine typhus.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss rodent control measures relevant to vector-borne disease control.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Rodent-proofing of storage, environmental sanitation, and rodenticide use, along with surveillance linked to NVBDCP activities.

spotter.Title: Spotter 3
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the food item and its nutrient group.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Sweet potato — root vegetable or tuber.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State one vitamin precursor it is rich in.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Rich in beta-carotene, a precursor of vitamin A.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss its relevance in a public health nutrition context.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Promoted as an accessible source to help address vitamin A deficiency, particularly where it is a locally grown staple.

spotter.Title: Spotter 4
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the food item and its category.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Double-fortified salt — fortified food.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State the two micronutrients it delivers.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Fortified with both iodine and iron.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss why combining two micronutrients in one vehicle is programmatically useful.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Addresses both iodine deficiency disorders and iron-deficiency anaemia through a single, widely consumed staple, simplifying delivery.

spotter.Title: Spotter 5
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the vaccine shown and state what it protects against.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Hepatitis A vaccine — protects against Hepatitis A infection.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State how the disease is typically transmitted.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Transmitted through the faeco-oral route, often via contaminated food or water.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss why this vaccine is not part of the free universal schedule in India.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Hepatitis A is generally self-limiting in children and improving sanitation is considered the primary long-term control strategy, so the vaccine remains optional.

spotter.Title: Spotter 6
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the equipment shown and state its purpose.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Vaccine carrier — used to transport vaccines to session sites, maintaining cold chain.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State how many ice packs it typically holds, and its approximate duration of cold retention.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Typically holds four ice packs and can maintain safe temperature for several hours during outreach sessions.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss its importance for outreach immunization.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Enables vaccines to be safely carried beyond fixed cold chain points to reach remote or mobile session sites.

spotter.Title: Spotter 7
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the method shown and its category.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Monthly injectable contraceptive — injectable method.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State its hormonal composition, and mention its frequency of administration.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: A combined estrogen-progestin injectable; administered once a month.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss one counselling point relevant to its use.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Requires monthly visits for injection, which may pose an adherence challenge for some clients.

spotter.Title: Spotter 8
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the combination shown and its category.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Condom used together with spermicide — barrier method.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: Explain why combining these two methods increases effectiveness.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: The condom provides a mechanical barrier while the spermicide adds a chemical barrier, together reducing the failure rate compared to either method alone.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss one counselling point relevant to this combined approach.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Both components should be used correctly and consistently with every act of intercourse to gain the added protective benefit.

spotter.Title: Spotter 9
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the diagram shown and state its purpose.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: Ergonomic workstation diagram — used to assess occupational postural risk factors.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: Name one postural risk factor it helps identify.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Incorrect monitor height, poor chair support, or improper desk height leading to musculoskeletal strain.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss its relevance in preventing occupational musculoskeletal disorders.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Guides workstation redesign to reduce repetitive strain injuries and chronic musculoskeletal complaints among office workers.

spotter.Title: Spotter 10
spotter.Sub_Question_A: Identify the health facility shown and state its position in the referral system.
spotter.Answer_Key_A: District Hospital — the apex referral facility at the district level.
spotter.Sub_Question_B: State the range of services typically available here.
spotter.Answer_Key_B: Provides comprehensive specialist, diagnostic, and emergency services beyond what CHCs can offer.
spotter.Sub_Question_C: Discuss its role in supporting the overall district health system.
spotter.Answer_Key_C: Acts as the final referral point within the district before a case would need referral to a tertiary-level institution.
